pairs.why: B keeps the real card's yellow background with orange pi marks and dark navy keys with cyan operator keys, while A's background is pushed toward orange and its keys are lighter and more purple.
A's water mass is the turquoise-to-teal of the real card, but its wood is a duller orange-brown than the real saturated orange; B spends much of the card on blue sky that the real card doesn't have.
A's deep indigo-navy hat against the warm orange background matches the real cards' rich navy-blue hero with a warm accent, while B's near-neutral black-grey hat has lost the chroma.
B has saturated, varied color (orange ground, purple sky, yellow glow, blue glass), like the real cards' high chroma, while A's gray lunar ground and white body are mostly neutral.
B's bottle is a softer, slightly translucent mid-blue on a yellow-to-orange burst closer to the real card, while A's blue is more saturated and its orange edges are hotter.
A has fewer hue families (green, blue sky, salmon path) like the real card, while B adds a red bench, pink flowers and a lamp, and both plants are lighter and more lime than the real dark green.
Both have the same yellow duck, red accents, blue base, orange sand and green burst background, with no meaningful palette difference.
Both use the same saturated green grass, lavender-gray stone, navy and cream board and blue sky, so color gives no reason to choose.
